# What is statistics? {#sec-introduction}

Statistics is the science of learning from data in the presence of
variability [@freedman2007].

::: {.callout-note}
## Key idea
A **population** is the full group we want to learn about; a **sample** is
the part of it we actually observe. A **parameter** describes the
population, a **statistic** describes the sample.
:::

## Notation

| Quantity      | Population (parameter) | Sample (statistic) |
|---------------|:----------------------:|:------------------:|
| Mean          | $\mu$                  | $\bar{x}$          |
| Std. deviation| $\sigma$               | $s$                |
| Proportion    | $p$                    | $\hat{p}$          |

: Notation used throughout the book {#tbl-notation}

See @tbl-notation; descriptive summaries are developed in
@sec-describing-data.

## Exercises

1. Give an example of a population and a sample from your own experience.
